newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil ops normal despite strike - PDVSA.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil ops normal despite strike - PDVSA.

text.p: Venezuela's oil industry maintained normal operations Wednesday despite a national strike that paralyzed much of the country, said a spokeswoman for state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA).

"Our contingency plan was brought into operation at 11 o'clock last night, and professional workers have assumed control of operations," she told Reuters by telephone. "The strike is going ahead without any problem and continued operations have been ensured by higher-level employees."
The 12-hour stoppage was called by Confederation of Venezuela Workers (CTV), Venezuela's largest union, to protest the private sector's failure to raise salaries.
Carlos Ortega, president of the main oil union Fedepetrol, said up to 60,000 oil workers would join the strike.
It was not clear what proportion of workers had respected the call to stay away from work.
In previous strikes, PDVSA has succesfully maintained its 3.2 million barrel per day operation using its "contingency plan" where professional employees replace striking workers.
